profile.research_note: [process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Vantage Data Centers cluster is in Sterling, Virginia, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn data center corridor. Vantage own site states the company began planning a 146 megawatt mega campus in Ashburn in October 2017, completing the first phase in February 2019 with 6 megawatts of IT capacity as an initial delivery. Vantage Data Centers was established in June 2010 with an investment from Silver Lake Partners, and Sureel Choksi became President and CEO in July 2013. DigitalBridge acquired Vantage in March 2017, and Silver Lake co-led a 9.2 billion dollar equity investment completed in June 2024. No building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Vantage VA2 in Sterling publishes 96 MW of IT capacity, ranking third among Virginia facilities with disclosed megawatt figures and representing roughly 7 percent of the 1,326 MW total published across 19 sites in the state.

Ninety-six megawatts of IT load is substantial for AI workloads. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common density for current AI training deployments, 96 MW supports roughly 2,400 racks. At 10 kW per rack, typical for general enterprise compute, the same power fills roughly 9,600 racks. These are assumptions about density, not operator claims. The published spec does not state rack count or supported density.

VA2 sits in the highest tier of disclosed capacity in Virginia, which is the densest concentration of data center infrastructure in the United States by mapped count. A 96 MW campus in that market is large enough to serve as a building block for hyperscale or large-model AI workloads, provided power delivery and network interconnection meet required specifications. Neither of those is confirmed by available data. The operator page does not publish certifications, tenant names, pricing, or connectivity details.
